review.why: The PR removes the application-level email uniqueness validation that prevents users from registering or updating their profile with an email already in use, relying solely on a database constraint which will surface as a 500 error instead of a clear 400 validation error.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description doesn't announce this change. The PR description explicitly states the email uniqueness check is redundant because the database enforces it, and the diff removes the validate_email method that produced the 'Use a different email.' error.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description doesn't announce this change. The PR description explicitly states the email uniqueness check is redundant because the database enforces it, and the diff removes the validate_email method that produced the 'Use a different email.' error.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description doesn't announce this change. The PR description announces removing the application-level email uniqueness validation, so the database now raises a UNIQUE constraint error instead of the custom validation error, which is the direct consequence of relying on the DB constraint.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description doesn't announce this change. The PR description announces removing the application-level email uniqueness validation, so the database now raises a UNIQUE constraint error instead of the custom validation error, which is the direct consequence of relying on the DB constraint.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR intentionally removes the application-level email uniqueness validation, replacing custom 'Use a different email.' errors with database UNIQUE constraint errors for both registration and profile updates.

suspicions.claim: Registering a new user with an email that already exists in the database now returns a 400 database integrity error instead of a 400 validation error with a clear message.
suspicions.trigger: POST /api/users with JSON {"username": "newuser", "email": "alice@example.com", "password": "pass"} where alice@example.com already exists; observe 400 response with code 400 and message 'Database integrity error' instead of validation error 'Use a different email.'
suspicions.evidence: probe_s1 POST /api/users with duplicate email returned base 400 validation error 'Use a different email.' and head 400 database integrity error 'UNIQUE constraint failed: users.email' with message 'Database integrity error'

suspicions.claim: Updating the authenticated user's email to an email already used by another user now returns a 400 database integrity error instead of a 400 validation error with a clear message.
suspicions.trigger: POST /api/tokens with basic auth alice:doppel-pass to get token; PUT /api/me with Authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON {"email": "bob@example.com"} where bob@example.com exists; observe 400 response with code 400 and message 'Database integrity error' instead of validation error 'Use a different email.'
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe_s2_duplicate_email_update PUT /api/me with duplicate email returned base 400 validation error 'Use a different email.' and head 400 database integrity error 'UNIQUE constraint failed: users.email' with message 'Database integrity error'

suspicions.claim: Updating the authenticated user's email to the same email they already have now triggers a database integrity error instead of being allowed as a no-op.
suspicions.trigger: POST /api/tokens with basic auth alice:doppel-pass to get token; PUT /api/me with Authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON {"email": "alice@example.com"} (same as current); observe 400 response with code 400 and message 'Database integrity error' instead of 200 OK with unchanged email.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s3 PUT /api/me with same email returned base 200 OK and head 200 OK, both allowing the no-op update without database integrity error
